   223	theorem exponential_to_surjective {X : Type*} [AddCommGroup X] {g : ℕ}
   224	    (u : GenusTorusUniformization X g) : Function.Surjective (exponential_to u) := by
   225	  intro x
   226	  obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := genusTorusExponential_surjective g (u.equiv x)
   227	  refine ⟨y, ?_⟩
   228	  change u.equiv.symm (genusTorusExponential g y) = x

   235	  ext x

   238	  · intro hx
   239	    change u.equiv.symm (genusTorusExponential g x) = 0 at hx
   240	    have hx' : genusTorusExponential g x = 0 := by
   241	      apply u.equiv.symm.injective
   242	      simpa only [map_zero] using hx
   243	    have hx'' : x ∈ (genusTorusExponential g).ker := (AddMonoidHom.mem_ker).mpr hx'

   246	  · intro hx
   247	    have hx' : x ∈ (genusTorusExponential g).ker := by
   248	      rw [genusTorusExponential_ker g]
   249	      exact hx
   250	    have hx'' : genusTorusExponential g x = 0 := (AddMonoidHom.mem_ker).mp hx'
   251	    change u.equiv.symm (genusTorusExponential g x) = 0

    19	/-- A real product torus, represented as a product of unit additive circles.
    20	
    21	This is the elementary real Lie-group model used in the proof of Mumford's
    22	divisibility and torsion proposition (`mumford-frag-torsion`).

    24	abbrev ProductTorus (d : Type*) := UnitAddTorus d

    26	/-- Every product torus admits division by a nonzero integer. -/
    27	theorem productTorus_division {d : Type*} (x : ProductTorus d) {n : ℤ} (hn : n ≠ 0) :
    28	    n • DivisibleBy.div x n = x :=
    29	  DivisibleBy.div_cancel x hn

    31	/-- Membership in the `n`-torsion of a product torus is coordinatewise. -/
    32	theorem mem_productTorus_torsion_iff {d : Type*} {n : ℕ} (x : ProductTorus d) :
    33	    x ∈ {x : ProductTorus d | n • x = 0} ↔ ∀ i, n • x i = 0 := by
    34	  constructor
    35	  · intro hx i
    36	    have hi := congrFun hx i
    37	    simpa only [Pi.smul_apply, Pi.zero_apply] using hi
    38	  · intro hx
    39	    change n • x = 0
    40	    funext i
    41	    exact hx i
    42	
    43	/-- Membership in integer-scalar torsion of a product torus is coordinatewise. -/
    44	theorem mem_productTorus_zsmul_torsion_iff {d : Type*} {n : ℤ} (x : ProductTorus d) :
    45	    x ∈ {x : ProductTorus d | n • x = 0} ↔ ∀ i, n • x i = 0 := by
    46	  constructor
    47	  · intro hx i
    48	    have hi := congrFun hx i
    49	    simpa only [Pi.smul_apply, Pi.zero_apply] using hi
    50	  · intro hx
    51	    change n • x = 0
    52	    funext i
    53	    exact hx i

    55	/-- The `n`-torsion of a finite product torus is finite. -/
    56	theorem productTorus_torsion_finite {d : Type*} [Finite d] {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) :
    57	    {x : ProductTorus d | n • x = 0}.Finite := by
    58	  have hpi : (Set.univ.pi (fun _ : d => {u : UnitAddCircle | n • u = 0})).Finite :=
    59	    Set.Finite.pi (fun i => AddCircle.finite_torsion (1 : ℝ) hn)
    60	  apply hpi.subset
    61	  intro x hx
    62	  simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq] at hx ⊢
    63	  intro i _
    64	  change n • x i = 0
    65	  have hi := congrFun hx i
    66	  simpa only [Pi.smul_apply, Pi.zero_apply] using hi

    68	private theorem real_isSMulRegular_int (n : ℤ) (hn : n ≠ 0) : IsSMulRegular ℝ n := by
    69	  exact .of_right_eq_zero_of_smul (fun (x : ℝ) (h : n • x = 0) => by
    70	    rw [zsmul_eq_mul] at h
    71	    have hc : (n : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast hn
    72	    rcases mul_eq_zero.mp h with h0 | hx
    73	    · exact (hc h0).elim
    74	    · exact hx)

    76	/-- The nonzero-integer torsion of a finite product torus is finite. -/
    77	theorem productTorus_zsmul_torsion_finite {d : Type*} [Finite d] {n : ℤ} (hn : n ≠ 0) :
    78	    {x : ProductTorus d | n • x = 0}.Finite := by
    79	  have hpi :
    80	      (Set.univ.pi (fun _ : d => {u : UnitAddCircle | n • u = 0})).Finite :=
    81	    Set.Finite.pi (fun _ => AddCircle.finite_torsion_of_isSMulRegular_int
    82	      (1 : ℝ) n (real_isSMulRegular_int n hn))
    83	  apply hpi.subset
    84	  intro x hx
    85	  simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq] at hx ⊢
    86	  intro i _
    87	  change n • x i = 0
    88	  have hi := congrFun hx i
    89	  simpa only [Pi.smul_apply, Pi.zero_apply] using hi

    91	/-!
    92	The quotient description of the additive circle gives an explicit model for
    93	its finite torsion.  We keep the equivalence at the subtype level so that the
    94	annihilation equation remains available to coordinatewise constructions.
    95	-/
    96	
    97	/-- The `n`-torsion of the unit additive circle is `ZMod n`. -/
    98	def unitAddCircle_torsion_equiv_zmod {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) :
    99	    {u : UnitAddCircle | n • u = 0} ≃ ZMod n := by
   100	  letI : NeZero n := ⟨Nat.ne_of_gt hn⟩
   101	  have hmem (j : ZMod n) : n • ZMod.toAddCircle j = 0 := by
   102	    apply (AddCircle.nsmul_eq_zero_iff hn).2
   103	    refine ⟨j.val, j.val_lt, ?_⟩
   104	    rw [ZMod.toAddCircle_apply]
   105	    norm_num
   106	  let f : ZMod n → {u : UnitAddCircle | n • u = 0} :=
   107	    fun j => ⟨ZMod.toAddCircle j, hmem j⟩
   108	  have hf : Function.Bijective f := by
   109	    constructor
   110	    · intro a b hab
   111	      exact ZMod.toAddCircle_injective n (Subtype.mk.inj hab)
   112	    · intro u
   113	      obtain ⟨m, hm, hu⟩ := (AddCircle.nsmul_eq_zero_iff hn).1 u.property
   114	      refine ⟨(m : ZMod n), ?_⟩
   115	      apply Subtype.ext
   116	      change ZMod.toAddCircle (m : ZMod n) = u.val
   117	      rw [ZMod.toAddCircle_apply]
   118	      simpa [Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hm] using hu
   119	  exact (Equiv.ofBijective f hf).symm
   120	
   121	/-- The torsion of a product torus is the corresponding product of `ZMod`s. -/
   122	def productTorus_torsion_equiv_pi_zmod {d : Type*} {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) :
   123	    {x : ProductTorus d | n • x = 0} ≃ (d → ZMod n) := by
   124	  let e := unitAddCircle_torsion_equiv_zmod hn
   125	  let f : (d → ZMod n) → {x : ProductTorus d | n • x = 0} := fun z =>
   126	    ⟨fun i => (e.symm (z i)).val, by
   127	      apply (mem_productTorus_torsion_iff (n := n) (fun i => (e.symm (z i)).val)).2
   128	      intro i
   129	      exact (e.symm (z i)).property⟩
   130	  have hf : Function.Bijective f := by
   131	    constructor
   132	    · intro a b hab
   133	      funext i
   134	      have hi : (e.symm (a i)).val = (e.symm (b i)).val :=
   135	        congrFun (Subtype.mk.inj hab) i
   136	      have heq : e.symm (a i) = e.symm (b i) := Subtype.ext hi
   137	      simpa using congrArg e heq
   138	    · intro x
   139	      have hx : ∀ i, n • x.val i = 0 :=
   140	        (mem_productTorus_torsion_iff (n := n) x.val).1 x.property
   141	      refine ⟨fun i => e ⟨x.val i, hx i⟩, ?_⟩
   142	      apply Subtype.ext
   143	      funext i
   144	      change (e.symm (e ⟨x.val i, hx i⟩)).val = x.val i
   145	      exact congrArg Subtype.val (e.symm_apply_apply ⟨x.val i, hx i⟩)
   146	  exact (Equiv.ofBijective f hf).symm
   147	
   148	/-- The finite `n`-torsion of a finite product torus has cardinality `n ^ |d|`. -/
   149	theorem productTorus_torsion_card {d : Type*} [Fintype d] {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) :
   150	    Nat.card {x : ProductTorus d | n • x = 0} = n ^ Fintype.card d := by
   151	  rw [Nat.card_congr (productTorus_torsion_equiv_pi_zmod hn)]
   152	  rw [Nat.card_fun, Nat.card_zmod, Nat.card_eq_fintype_card]

     9	# Translation isomorphisms and transport of point-local properties (Wave-5 X2)
    10	
    11	Group schemes are homogeneous: right translation by a point is an automorphism, so any
    12	point-local property that holds at one rational point spreads to every rational point.
    13	This file provides the translation isomorphisms and the transport lemmas that the
    14	Wave-5 smoothness lane consumes — S1 (spreading geometric reducedness from the
    15	identity section, recon route α1) and S3 (uniformizing the fibre dimension across the
    16	smooth locus) — plus the `JacobianData` corollaries for `d.J`.
    17	
    18	Mathlib's `AlgebraicGeometry/Group/Smooth.lean` performs the same homogeneity dance,
    19	but INLINE inside the `private` lemma `smooth_of_grpObj_of_isAlgClosed` (there are no
    20	reusable standalone lemmas there — checked against the pinned checkout).  Per the
    21	worksheet mandate we therefore re-prove the minimal general forms here instead of
    22	copying the private proof wholesale.
    23	
    24	## Contents
    25	
    26	* Categorical layer (any cartesian monoidal category, Hom-group calculus):
    27	  `GrpObj.comp_mulRight_hom` / `comp_mulRight_inv` — composing with a right
    28	  translation is Hom-group multiplication; `GrpObj.pointTranslation x y : G ≅ G` — the
    29	  translation `(· ⋅ x⁻¹ y)` carrying the point `x` to the point `y`
    30	  (`comp_pointTranslation_hom`).
    31	* Scheme layer: `pointTranslationIso G x y : G.left ≅ G.left` — the same translation
    32	  as an isomorphism of the underlying scheme of a group scheme `G : Over S`, with its
    33	  structure-morphism compatibility (`pointTranslationIso_hom_comp`) and its action on
    34	  the underlying points (`pointTranslationIso_hom_apply`).
    35	* Transport of point-local properties along automorphisms/open immersions —
    36	  `mem_smoothLocus_iff_of_comp_eq` (membership in the smooth locus),
    37	  `isReduced_stalk_iff_of_isOpenImmersion` (reducedness of the stalk),
    38	  `isIrreducible_preimage_iff_of_isIso` (irreducibility of subsets, in particular of
    39	  open neighbourhoods).
    40	* `JacobianData` corollaries closing the file: `d.pointTranslation`,
    41	  `d.pointTranslationIso`, and the three transport statements specialized to `d.J`.
    42	-/

     8	/-!
     9	# FIELD-POINT RIGIDITY IS A STATEMENT ABOUT TEST ALGEBRAS
    10	
    11	`Picard/Pic0VanishingRigidityReduction.lean` proved that at `genus C = 0` the `pic⁰` vanishing
    12	`hvan` — the hypothesis both live routes to a `rep` producer pass through — is **equivalent** to
    13	field-point rigidity of `picEt`:
    14	
    15	  `hrig`: a `picEt C T` class restricting to `1` at every field point of `T` is `1`.
    16	
    17	`hrig` still quantifies over all test *objects*.  This file removes that quantifier: it is
    18	enough to have the statement at affine tests, in the plus-class spelling
    19	
    20	  `hrigAff`: a `PicEtAff C A` class with `PicEtAff.mapAlg C φ q = 1` for every `φ : A →ₐ[k] K`
    21	  into a field is `1`,
    22	
    23	and the reduction is `rigidity_of_rigidityAff` below — with its converse
    24	`rigidityAff_of_rigidity`, so the two are the **same** hypothesis
    25	(`rigidity_iff_rigidityAff`).  Composed with the equivalence of the previous file,
    26	`subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_of_rigidityAff` derives the vanishing at **every** test object from a
    27	statement in which no scheme, no open and no morphism of schemes occurs — only commutative
    28	`k`-algebras and algebra maps into fields.
    29	
    30	## The mechanism
    31	
    32	Two independent halves, and neither is a quantifier trick.
    33	
    34	**The componentwise half** is the same observation that makes `subsingleton_picEt_of_affine`
    35	one line: `picEt C T` is a subgroup of the *product* of the `PicEtAff C Γ(T.left, U)` over the
    36	affine opens `U` of `T.left`, so `picEt.ext` reduces `lam = 1` to `lam.1 U = 1` at each `U`.
    37	
    38	**The field-point half is the content**, and it runs the other way: `hrigAff` at
    39	`A := Γ(T.left, U)` needs the hypothesis at every algebra map `φ : Γ(T.left, U) →ₐ[k] K`, and
    40	what `hrig`'s hypothesis supplies are field points of `T`.  The bridge is the *composite*
    41	
    42	  `Over.overSpecMap φ ≫ Over.fromSpecAffine T U : overSpec k K ⟶ T`,
    43	
    44	a genuine field point of `T`, together with three coherences: `picEtMap_comp` splits the
    45	restriction; `picEtAffineEquiv_naturality` turns the outer leg into `PicEtAff.mapAlg C φ`; and
    46	`picEtMapVal_eq_mapAlg` identifies the inner leg's value at the *top* affine open of
    47	`overSpec k Γ(T.left, U)` with `mapAlg` of `Over.appLEAlgHom` applied to `lam.1 U` — legitimate
    48	because `⊤ ≤ fromSpec ⁻¹ᵁ U` (`IsAffineOpen.fromSpec_preimage_self`,
    49	`top_le_preimage_fromSpecAffine` here).
    50	
    51	What is left is the bookkeeping identity `fromSpecAffine_ΓTop_comp_appLEAlgHom`:
    52	`Γ`-`Spec` transport composed with the `appLE` of `fromSpec` is the identity on
    53	`Γ(T.left, U)`.  That is `IsAffineOpen.fromSpec_app_of_le` at `le_rfl` plus
    54	`ΓSpecIso.inv_hom_id`, and it is worth its own name because it is the only place where the
    55	`Spec`-`Γ` adjunction enters — a consumer relating an evaluation of `picEt` to a restriction
    56	along `fromSpecAffine` will need it again.
    57	
    58	## What this does NOT do
    59	
    60	* **It does not prove `hrigAff`, at any curve.**  The statement remains without a producer; what
    61	  changes is that the surviving obligation is now spelled entirely in commutative algebra.  Per
    62	  `I-1650` this is a **statability** gain, not a shrinking of the obligation — the imported
    63	  equivalence one layer down is between two spellings of one hypothesis.
    64	* **The bookkeeping is not what carries the headline.**  Recorded because an audit (`I-1652`)
    65	  measured it: `subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_of_rigidityAff` also follows from the *pre-session*
    66	  `Pic0VanishingAffineReduction` + `Pic0VanishingFieldTest` pair, bypassing
    67	  `top_le_preimage_fromSpecAffine`, `fromSpecAffine_ΓTop_comp_appLEAlgHom` and
    68	  `picEtMapVal_eq_mapAlg` entirely.  What those three buy is the **general-`T`** form of
    69	  `rigidity_of_rigidityAff` (and hence `rigidity_iff_rigidityAff`), which the affine-only route
    70	  does not give.  That is a real generality gain and it is not the vanishing.
    71	* It says nothing at positive genus; the genus hypothesis enters only through the imported
    72	  equivalence, not through anything in this file.
    73	
    74	## Main declarations
    75	
    76	* `AlgebraicGeometry.top_le_preimage_fromSpecAffine` — the top affine open of
    77	  `overSpec k Γ(T.left, U)` lies in the `fromSpecAffine`-preimage of `U`.
    78	* `AlgebraicGeometry.fromSpecAffine_ΓTop_comp_appLEAlgHom` — the `Spec`-`Γ` bookkeeping
    79	  identity, isolated.
    80	* `AlgebraicGeometry.rigidity_of_rigidityAff` — **the reduction**: rigidity at test algebras
    81	  gives rigidity at test objects.
    82	* `AlgebraicGeometry.rigidityAff_of_rigidity` — the converse, and
    83	  `AlgebraicGeometry.rigidity_iff_rigidityAff` the equivalence, so the affine form is not
    84	  stronger.
    85	* `AlgebraicGeometry.subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_of_rigidityAff` — the `pic⁰` vanishing at every
    86	  test object from a purely ring-level hypothesis, at genus `0`.
    87	* `AlgebraicGeometry.P1.subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_of_rigidityAff` — the same at `ℙ¹`, with the
    88	  genus hypothesis discharged.
    89	-/

   147	identity above.
